data.narrative:
Field AI, an AI & Software company founded by Ali Agha and Shayegan Omidshafiei, is evaluated here at Series B stage against a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company (Palantir; ticker PLTR). The private peer set includes Scale AI, Physical Intelligence, Black Forest Labs, and Figure AI, providing direct stage and sector alignment.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchored to the company's last post-money valuation of $2.0B, applies a typical Series B-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.9x, implying a valuation of $3.8B. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same-stage comparables: Scale AI at $29.0B, Physical Intelligence at $5.6B, and Black Forest Labs at $3.2B. The median of this set is $5.6B, though the range spans $3.2B to $29.0B, reflecting wide dispersion typical of high-growth AI companies.

Triangulating these two methods yields a supported range of $3.2B to $6.4B, with a median of $4.7B. This suggests Field AI's current $2.0B valuation sits below the implied midpoint. Key uncertainties center on the extreme outlier (Scale AI at $29.0B) and the degree to which the peer set reflects true operational and market comparability. The wide peer range underscores the volatility inherent in valuing early-stage AI companies absent established revenue benchmarks.
